page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 48.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on the x86_64 architecture.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for most workloads, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 23333.53 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12002.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1266.21 GB/sec, dropping to 129.2 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Notably, the instance demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small LLM models, achieving 295.58 tokens/sec, which falls into the top 25% category. Other operations, such as Redis SET operations at 23.57 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 27.72 GB/sec, remain in the average range.

Given its compute-to-memory ratio and lack of bundled local storage, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe drives. It is appropriate for tasks such as software compilation, where it scored 21392.0 on Geekbench clang compilation, as well as web serving, lightweight database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.6xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs (12 physical cores) from an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, paired with 48.0 GB of RAM. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Benchmark results show average performance across standard CPU and memory tests, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 23333.53 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12002.0. However, it exhibits strong performance in text generation for small language models, reaching 295.58 tokens/sec. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy, memory-light workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and static web serving.
